blogPosts.title: Dialing in Launch Angle & Spin Rates on Indian Championship Fairways
blogPosts.excerpt: How course elevation, morning dew, and grass density in Delhi, Bangalore, and Mumbai dictate your clubhead setup.
blogPosts.author: Gaurav Khanna, Head Fitting Specialist
blogPosts.content:
Indian golf courses present diverse micro-climates. From the morning dew and bentgrass greens of Prestige Golfshire in Bangalore to the undulating kikuyu turf and high humidity at the Royal Calcutta Golf Club, one driver configuration does not suit every venue.

When setting up your driver for Indian conditions, launch angle and spin rates become the defining variables. For players averaging 95 to 105 mph swing speeds, aiming for a launch angle between 12.5° and 14.2° with backspin between 2,100 and 2,400 RPM produces the optimum combination of carry distance and roll-out.

Shaft stiffness and tip profile play an equally vital role. Fujikura Ventus profiles featuring VeloCore technology stabilize the clubhead through maximum rotational torque, reducing dispersion on tight tree-lined corridors like Delhi Golf Club's famous bush-lined fairways.

blogPosts.title: Cast vs. Forged Irons: Dissecting Acoustics, Feel, and Turf Interaction
blogPosts.excerpt: Why master players gravitate toward Japanese Grain Flow Forged irons and how modern dual-cavity technology provides forgiveness.
blogPosts.author: Climate Change Digital Labs Tech Desk
blogPosts.content:
The debate between forged and cast iron construction has intrigued golfers for decades. At The House of Gaunt, we look at the metallurgical science behind the strike.

Forging involves heating a solid billet of 1025E mild carbon steel and compressing it under hydraulic hammers up to 1,000 tons of pressure. This aligns the molecular grain structure of the steel consistently across the head, damping harsh vibrations upon impact.

Conversely, investment casting pours molten steel into ceramic molds. Casting allows perimeter weighting and ultra-thin faces, but traditional cast stainless steel has a higher resonant frequency—often perceived by players as a "clicky" or rigid strike. Modern engineering has bridged this gap with tungsten perimeter weighting welded onto a forged chassis.

blogPosts.title: Preserving Tour-Grade Cabretta Leather Gloves in Tropical Climates
blogPosts.excerpt: Simple maintenance rituals to prevent leather crusting and double the lifespan of your tour gloves.
blogPosts.author: Ananya Deshmukh, Apparel Curator
blogPosts.content:
AAA Cabretta sheepskin leather offers exceptional grip because of its porous natural lipid structure. However, exposure to perspiration, sunscreen lotions, and high humidity during Indian summer rounds can harden the leather if not properly stored.

Always alternate between two gloves during a single round in peak summer. Keep a glove shaper or lay the glove flat on the exterior of your golf bag's Velcro patch rather than crumpling it inside a dark zipper compartment. Never dry leather gloves under direct sunlight or with artificial heat sources.
